acceptance.claimBoundary: Acceptance proves that consequential transitions require artifact-bound human authority; it does not establish external identity-provider assurance.
evidenceRequired: Automated tests reject altered, expired, replayed, mismatched, wrong-scope, and agent-authored receipts.
A repository owner reviews the allowed authority roles and transition matrix.

completionCriteria: Premise agreement is session-bound and digest-bound to the exact assumption presented to the operator.
Canonical backlog adoption, execution-capable handoff approval, outcome promotion, and retirement each require a separately typed human decision receipt.
Human receipts identify an allowed repository authority, bind the exact artifact digest and repository revision, state their scope, and enforce expiry or supersession where applicable.
Agent identities cannot approve execution, select an arena winner, promote institutional learning, or retire an accepted decision.
Generic memory and handoff commands cannot bypass the required ratification lifecycle.
Altered, expired, replayed, mismatched, agent-authored, and wrong-scope receipts fail closed in automated tests.
nonObjectives: Do not claim cryptographic human identity without an approved identity-provider boundary.
Do not permit an agent, model, or UI checkbox to substitute for repository authority.
Do not rewrite or delete historical decision and outcome records.
objective: Make every consequential Proofloom approval durable, artifact-bound, human-owned, and non-bypassable.
title: Harden human authority and ratification gates
